title: weightstream-mmap-fallback-logbook
content:
Goal: collect breadcrumbs for intermittent model load failures during Canary A that seem to be related to: partial downloads, mmap fallback, and inconsistent shard metadata.

Summary of observed behavior:
- 2024-11-01 Canary A (model: rdm-large-v2, pinned v2024-10-29) had ~3/70 starts fail to reach READY.
- Failures occur within first 10s of process start; serving runtime logs show `KVCache init` then abrupt failure during weight map stage.
- Symptoms: process exits with code 139 (segfault) or raises OSError: [Errno 22] Invalid argument when attempting mmap on a weights shard file.
- On hosts where it fails, /tmp/weights streaming shows file sizes ~10–20 bytes smaller than expected (reported by manifest).

Commands I ran (local repro and on instance):
$ gsutil cp gs://redwood-weights/rdm-large-v2/v2024-10-29/manifest.json ./
$ cat manifest.json | jq .shards | wc -l
70

# stream download attempt to avoid full tarball
$ python -c "import sys,requests; r=requests.get('https://storage.redwood/rdm-large-v2/part-001', stream=True); open('part-001','wb').write(r.raw.read())"
# partial write reproduces truncated file, size mismatch seen in stat output

On-host runtime start (trimmed logs):
[2024-11-01T09:03:14Z] INFO core: begin weight assembly
[2024-11-01T09:03:14Z] DEBUG storage:gcs: open stream for shard part-033 (expected 1.2GB)
[2024-11-01T09:03:24Z] WARN storage:gcs: read returned 1342177000 bytes (manifest expects 1342177280) -> retry
[2024-11-01T09:03:24Z] DEBUG weight-loader: compute sha256 for part-033: tmpfile -> mismatch
[2024-11-01T09:03:24Z] ERROR weight-loader: mmap fallback attempt for /mnt/weights/rdm/v2024-10-29/part-033
OSError: [Errno 22] Invalid argument
# process crashes shortly after; no stacktrace from C++ layer in logs, but core dump exists

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) GCS range/stream responses occasionally short on a single TCP chunk; our streaming reader treats a short read as EOF and leaves truncated file on disk. Later mmap fails because file isn't page-aligned to expected length or file header is corrupt.
2) Manifest-level metadata (size + sha256) sometimes computed from a compressed intermediate (e.g., stored gz) but we compare against decompressed size, causing mismatch and triggering fallback logic in the loader that assumes a whole-file atomic write.
3) mmap flags/permissions differ across kernel versions (some nodes run 5.4 vs 6.x): MAP_PRIVATE with offset not page-aligned will raise EINVAL. Our code may call mmap with the wrong offset when reassembling shards from tar stream.
4) Race between stream write and mmap: mmap attempted on a file still being flushed (fsync not yet done) especially when writing to XFS on tmpfs.

Small experiments and findings:
- Reproduced truncated download by killing stream at 98%: when retries were enabled, the code appended instead of overwriting, resulting in a final file larger but with repeated footer bytes. After that, sha256 check fails — unit repro succeeded.
- Verified kernel error mapping: quick test on node kernels (5.4 vs 6.1) shows mmap with non-page-aligned offset returns EINVAL on both. So kernel version unlikely to be the differentiator here.
- When I force fsync and close before mmap in a small Python script, the mmap call succeeds consistently. Suspect our C++ loader may not fsync/close in the exact order when streaming into the final path.

Code locations to inspect (notes):
- runtime/storage/gcs_stream_reader.cc: read loop + handling of short reads; check whether it treats short read as EOF only when Content-Length missing.
- runtime/weights/assembly.cc: path where mmap is attempted; search for use of posix_fallocate, fsync, close ordering.
- runtime/weights/checksum.cc: sha256 vs manifest comparison; verify whether expected_size is compressed or raw.

Immediate mitigation applied to Canary A (2024-11-03):
- Disable mmap fallback for the canary (force loader to use buffered read into preallocated file + fsync). Decreased crash rate to 0/100 starts over 24h. That suggests mmap path was involved.
- Add extra verification step: after streaming each shard, stat(size) == expected_size, else delete and retry. This reduced partial-file artifacts but did not eliminate the underlying streaming anomaly.

Notes on observed errors and decoded meanings:
- "read returned X bytes (manifest expects Y) -> retry": indicates a reported short read from GCS library. Could be transient but needs safe handling (temp files, retries with overwrite, not append).
- OSError: [Errno 22] Invalid argument during mmap: typically offset/page alignment or invalid length. If the file is truncated, requesting mmap length > file size also yields EINVAL.
- Exit code 139 w/o nice stacktrace: segfault likely in native code doing pointer math after mmap; need core dump symbolization (gdb) to confirm exact instruction.

Debugging next steps / TODOs:
- [ ] Add verbose logging in gcs_stream_reader.cc to log Content-Range, bytes read per read() call, and whether we append vs overwrite on retry. Link with request IDs.
- [ ] Change streaming write behavior: write to temp file with random suffix, atomic rename to final path only after full size + checksum validated. This avoids mmap racing with incomplete files.
- [ ] Add an fsync() before mmap in assembly.cc and ensure file descriptor not opened with O_DIRECT unless supported.
- [ ] Add a small kernel-level smoke test suite that runs on all image types: write a large file with multiple short write() calls then attempt mmap from a different process to simulate race.
- [ ] Re-run Canary with mmap disabled for 48h then re-enable with additional guards (atomic rename + fsync) in a canary build.
- [ ] If short reads persist, escalate to GCS storage infra to check for network/edge issues during large object reads; gather tcpdump traces.

Notes-to-self about reproduction attempts:
- Repro script used: tools/dev/repro_weight_stream.py (local) — can be run with --simulate-short-read N to create truncated shards.
- Core dumps are stored: /var/crash/rdm-canary-nodes/*.core (need symbols from build-2024-10-29).
- When attaching gdb: use `gdb --args ./runtime --config canary.json` then run to reproduce; after segfault, `bt full` shows assembly.cc:line ~312 as top of stack on one host.

Open questions:
- Why does GCS sometimes return a short read? Intermittent network errors vs streaming library bug?
- Do we have any older nodes still running a pre-fix of the GCS client lib? (check version in /opt/redwood/lib/gcs-client/manifest.txt)
- Are shards stored with any gzip/transfer-encoding that our reader mistakenly treats as raw blob?

If I had to pick a next single most useful change: implement atomic write+fsync+rename in storage layer and re-enable mmap with that protection. If that eliminates crashes, we can conclude race/truncation was root cause.

End log. Will update after I instrument the reader and run the 48h canary.

-- Leo
